reason: Starts in a side gully just below the Liberty Bell-Concord notch on the west side; every party walks the Blue Lake Trail and the Beckey gully, and the hairpin pullout serves the east face, not this start.
Starts at the Liberty Bell-Concord notch, reached only by the Blue Lake Trail and the Beckey gully; the hairpin pullout serves the east-face routes.
A west-face line approached from the Blue Lake Trail like the other west-side Liberty Bell routes; no source describes a hairpin-side approach for it.
Southwest-corner start reached from the Beckey gully (left at the fork) off the Blue Lake Trail; the hairpin pullout serves the east face only.
The traverse starts up the Beckey Route and descends South Early Winters Spire back into the Blue Lake basin, so it is a one-trailhead loop from Blue Lake.
East-face route started from the hairpin pond pullout like Liberty Crack and Thin Red Line; the Blue Lake side reaches the west face, not this start.
Shares the Beckey Route's first pitch, so the way in is the Blue Lake Trail and the Beckey gully (right at the fork).

Every recorded north-ridge ascent comes up Wolf Creek to Gardner Meadows; the North Creek side is undescribed and the Scatter Lake trail reaches the south ridge, not this one. Stored pin taken from the row's own Wolf Creek Trailhead waypoint.
The south ridge is climbed from Scatter Lake off the Twisp River road; Wolf Creek leads to the north ridge, a separate route. Stored pin taken from the row's own Scatter Creek trailhead waypoint.

Both starts (the Ice Caves lot and the Dickerman pullout across the highway) are roadside points a short way apart that converge at the same South Fork log crossing, which the existing card already covers. Stored pin is the row's own Ice Caves waypoint.
Approached from the Big Four Picnic Area / Ice Caves trailhead like the peak's other technical routes; no second trailhead is described. Pin from the row's own waypoint.
North-face couloir directly above the Ice Caves nature trail; there is no other way to its base. Pin from the row's own waypoint.
North-side route reached from the Ice Caves trail; one trailhead. Pin from the row's own waypoint.

West-face route staged from the North Star-Bonanza col camp via Holden Village like its neighbours; the High Bridge sibling is Needle Peak, not Bonanza. Pin copied from sibling wa_bonanza_peak_mary_green_glacier's Holden Village / Railroad Creek Trailhead.
West-side line above the Southwest Rib start, reached from the Blue Lake Trail; the hairpin pullout serves the spire's east buttresses.
West/northwest face, same Blue Lake basin approach as Mojo Rising and the Northwest Face.
West/northwest face, reached from the Blue Lake Trail and the basin below the west face.
Approached as for The Passenger from the South Arete base via the Blue Lake Trail; no description of a hairpin-side approach to this southeast-face start.
Both ways onto the southwest side (over Sahale Arm, or down Pelton Basin and up the Horseshoe Basin trail) start at the Cascade Pass trailhead; Boston Basin serves the north face.
The couloir is gained straight up Spire Gully from the SR-20 hairpin; the Blue Lake side is the wrong side of the mountain.
East-side route approached from the hairpin pullout as for the Direct East Buttress; Blue Lake serves the west face.
West-face line sharing the Chockstone Route start, reached only from the Blue Lake Trail.

A winter/spring couloir reached from Narada Falls along the closed Reflection Lakes road; the Pinnacle Saddle trailhead on the same road is only a seasonal-gate difference, not a separate approach parties choose.
Same State Creek pullout and climbers' track as the South Buttress, just contouring lower to the toe; the 'state creek' and 'south buttress' pullouts are one place. Pin from the row's own waypoint.
East-face couloir reached from the State Creek pullout by crossing the rib into the east basin; one trailhead.
Same as its duplicate: the State Creek pullout, then over the rib into the basin east of the peak.
State Creek pullout and the basin south of the peak; one trailhead.

The East Face is reached from the SR-20 State Creek pullout, cutting up to the face once around the South Buttress base; the Rainy Pass option belongs to the North Ridge's northwest basin, not this face. Pin copied from sibling wa_cutthroat_peak_northeast_face.
All Wine Spires routes use the pullout across from the spires and the Burgundy Col climbers' trail.
The route is a ridge traverse that begins at the Cedar Creek / Early Winters confluence; the MP 166 pullout is only its descent finish, so there is one way onto it.

The ridge is reached from the Silver Star Glacier, and the glacier has two ways in from different SR-20 parking spots: the steep Burgundy Col climbers' path (stored) and the Silver Star Creek valley from the north, favoured on spring snow.

Stored approach is Burgundy Col then a traverse southwest; the Silver Star Creek approach from the north is a recognised snow-season way onto the glacier side, but nothing confirms parties use it for this rarely-in-condition face.
Approached via the Gato Negro descent gully on the Wine Spires side from the MP 166 pullout; the Silver Star Creek approach leads to the glacier, not this west-side couloir.
Goodell Creek to Terror Basin like the other Inspiration routes; the two Goodell Creek trailhead names are the same start.

The ridge starts from the basin between Emerald and Saska, which is reached either up the North Fork Entiat or by boat to Lucerne and up Emerald Park over Milham Pass; the sibling West Route already carries both, and this row's own camp list names Milham Pass. Stored pin from the row's own North Fork Entiat waypoint.
Boston Basin trailhead and high camp, then east around the basin; one trailhead.

All recorded ways to the Forbidden Glacier's north arm (round via the Boston Glacier, off the North Ridge, or from the West Ridge notch) start from Boston Basin; they are cards, not separate trailheads.

The route is climbed from Summerland via Fryingpan Creek; the White River Campground start is a forced detour while the Fryingpan trailhead is closed for bridge work, not a choice, and Paradise serves the separate Cowlitz-Ingraham route. Pin from the row's own waypoint.
The Conrad Glacier is on the South Fork Tieton (Conrad Meadows) side; Snowgrass Flat serves the west-side route. Pin from the row's own waypoint.
Reached from the North Fork Sauk via White Pass and Glacier Gap like the Sitkum and Frostbite routes; the old White Chuck approach remains washed out.

A northeast-face ice line from the Ice Cliff Glacier beside the Girth Pillar, so the way in is the Stuart Lake trailhead and Mountaineer Creek like those siblings; a winter road gate only lengthens that same approach. Pin copied from sibling wa_mount_stuart_ice_cliff_glacier.
This route IS the Cougar Divide approach; the Skyline Divide way is its own catalog route to the same summit block, so this row has one way in. Pin from the row's own waypoint.
Hannegan Pass over Ruth Mountain to the Ruth-Icy saddle; the campground and pass trailhead names are the same start.

Shares the Northwest Buttress's Upper Dungeness/Home Lake approach and first pitch; the Dosewallips start serves the standard route and is only met on this route's descent. Pin from the row's own waypoint.
The southwest ridge is reached by the old Little Jack trail off the East Bank Trail; Ross Lake/May Creek and Canyon Creek serve the north and south-side routes. Pin from the row's own waypoint.
Short approach from the PCT North trailhead onto the old Commonwealth Creek trail; one trailhead.
PCT north from Snoqualmie Pass; the two trailhead names are the same lot.
Tooth and Claw is on Lexington Tower's east side, which every party reaches from the hairpin pond pullout; the Blue Lake trailhead serves the west-facing lines of the group, not this one.

Lake Valhalla, the base of the scramble, is reached either from the Smithbrook trailhead via Union Gap or northbound on the crest trail from the Stevens Pass north lot; both are widely used, Stevens Pass especially when Smith Brook road is snowbound. Stevens Pass pin taken from the catalog's Stevens Pass North Lot trailhead on wa_sky_mountain_s_route.
The northwest face sits above the Thunder Glacier side and is reached only from the Heliotrope Ridge trailhead; the Middle Fork road leads to the southwest side and the X Couloir, not this face.

The row itself names two ways to the southwest face: the Middle Fork road and Rankin Creek (direct), or Heliotrope Ridge through the Thunder Glacier cirque. With the Middle Fork road closed by a washout at milepost 7 since July 2026, the Heliotrope start is a real choice. Heliotrope pin from sibling wa_lincoln_peak_north_ridge.
The south face is reached only through Commonwealth Basin from the PCT north trailhead; the Alpental start serves the west ridge from the Snow Lake side.

The couloir is approached from the White Salmon lot at the ski area, down to the valley and up the White Salmon side; the only other mention is a long ski-descent link-up over the summit from the Lake Ann side, not a way to climb it.

The loop can be started at either of two trailheads: most start at Killen Creek on the north side, others at Cold Springs on the south. The row has no stored way, so the Killen Creek start is n0; pins from sibling rows wa_mount_adams_lyman_glacier (Killen Creek) and wa_mount_adams_south_climb (Cold Springs).
Reached only by first climbing Mount Crowder by its one catalog route (Southwest Route) and continuing over; no separate way in and no second catalog route leads to it.

The row says Crowder is reached on multi-day Picket traverses from either Goodell Creek or the Big Beaver/Access Creek side, but no page found confirms which corridor parties actually use to reach Wild Lake for this route.
The north-face approach is undocumented; the row offers leaving the West Ridge path or a bushwhack from the Anderson Creek road, both off the same FR-62 system, and no page confirms either.
The route is defined by its Pinnacle Lake start up Iodine Gulch; the standard Pilchuck trailhead leads to the other side of the mountain.
Every party walks in from the Depot Creek road to the Ouzel Lake basin and starts the traverse from whichever summit it climbs first; that is a direction of travel, not a second way in.

All reports start at the Westside Road gate; Tahoma Creek and the Round Pass / South Puyallup line are two tracks from the same gate. The Mowich Lake link is a 26-mile Wonderland trek, not a climbing approach.
Climbers Bivouac in season; in winter the road is snow-gated and parties climb Worm Flows from the sno-park instead (a separate catalog route) rather than reaching Monitor Ridge another way.
Worm Flows is the Marble Mountain Sno-Park route by definition; the Climbers Bivouac start leads to Monitor Ridge, its own catalog route.
Tiffany Springs and trail #373 over Honeymoon Pass is the only way to the north-face cirque; the three drives all reach the same campground.
Same single approach as the NE Couloir: Tiffany Springs and trail #373 over Honeymoon Pass; the different drives converge on one trailhead.
The route is itself the Nason Ridge traverse from Old Merritt Lake over Mastiff and Howard; the Rock Mountain trail leads to the west route, not onto this ridge.

Two maintained trails from different trailheads reach the summit: the steep #1587 from US-2, and the Snowy Creek trail from FR-6705 off Smith Brook road, which joins the crest higher and is shorter with less gain. Snowy Creek pin from the trailhead page; FR-6705 has been closed by storm damage since June 2026.
The Dailey Prairie gate and the FR-38 gate at the Middle Fork bridge are the same place; all three Twin Sister routes share one approach into Orsino Creek Basin.
Same single approach as the other South Twin routes: the Middle Fork bridge gate, the logging roads and Orsino Creek Basin.

The east face was first reached by water taxi and Perry Creek, which is the row's card; the Depot Creek side is the usual way to Southeast Mox's other routes, but no page confirms parties reach the base of the east face from it (the row's only camp is on the Redoubt Glacier, the Depot Creek side, which is itself inconsistent).
Round Mountain trailhead is the practical way; reaching the lookout from Merritt Lake or along Nason Ridge is a much longer ridge hike done as a traverse.

The north ridge starts from Cathedral Pass, which is reached the same two ways as the West Route: Andrews Creek over Andrews Pass, or the Chewuch River trail from Thirtymile. Row has no cards, so the stored Andrews Creek way is n0; Thirtymile pin from sibling wa_amphitheater_mountain_north_buttress.

Reached from a Chain Lakes / Bullseye Pass camp, which parties reach from Stevens Pass via Josephine Lake and the Icicle Creek trail; walking up the Icicle from its road end is possible but much longer and rarely chosen.
Same single approach as the North Route: the Middle Fork Snoqualmie road on foot or bike from the Dingford Creek gate.
North Fork Entiat trailhead only; the Emerald Park / Milham Pass side from Lake Chelan is a multi-day alternative not used for this route.
Eightmile Lake to Lake Caroline and Windy Pass is the one way to the west ridge.
Graves Creek and the East Fork Quinault, the same approach as the standard route; no alternative way in.
Trinity and Chiwawa Basin is the standard way; the Phelps Creek card is a rarely used bushwhack variant, and the Phelps Creek road is under a storm-damage closure in 2026.
Canyon Creek and Jackita Ridge is the climbing approach; the Devils Dome loop card is a long backpacking circuit used only to avoid the ford.
One roadside pullout below the basin; Washington Pass's Blue Lake lot is only a meeting point for the same start.
The southwest scramble goes straight up from the Gorge Creek pull-off; the Stetattle Creek start from Diablo serves the north side.
Downey Creek and Bachelor Creek remains the recommended approach (now with a long bike on the closed Suiattle road); the Lake Chelan side adds a full day each way and is rarely used.
Phelps Creek to Spider Meadow and Phelps Basin; the Holden / Spider Gap line is used only by parties already on that loop.
This row is itself the Standup Creek way up Earl Peak, with one way in; the Beverly Turnpike start belongs to the separate Southwest Ridge route.
Normally from Rainy Pass on the crest trail to Snowy Lakes; the off-trail Swamp Creek start was a first-ascent choice, not a common alternative.
The ascent is by Lower Maynard Burn over Baldy; the Royal Basin card reaches the east face and serves as a traverse exit rather than a second way up this route.
One way in: the spur road end, then off trail up the drainage to Klinger Ridge.
Directly above Alpental Road via the ski track and south-side talus; the Commonwealth Basin start serves other aspects of the peak.
This row is itself one of Hadley's two approaches; the other (Cougar Divide) is its own sibling route.
The climb starts at the ranger station at the head of Ross Lake; the water taxi and the road from the north only differ in how you reach that one start.
Row is empty; the ridge is gained from the col between the peaks, reached from the head of Ross Lake like the other Hozomeen routes, with no known second way in.
All three cards lead to the same Hozomeen side of the lake; the water taxi and the northern road only change how you reach the campground, and the Lightning Creek line is rarely used.
Both cards start at the Dosewallips washout; one trailhead with two tracks. The Upper Dungeness start serves the northwest buttress.

The west face is reached from Lake Valhalla, which parties reach either from the Smith Brook road trailhead via Union Gap or on the crest trail north from Stevens Pass. Row has no cards, so the stored Smith Brook way is n0; the stored trailhead pin comes from this row's own Smithbrook waypoint, and the Stevens Pass pin from wa_sky_mountain_s_route.
Colchuck Lake and Aasgard Pass is the way up; the Snow Lakes route through the Enchantments is used by through-hikers and is far longer. The two cards are dry versus snowy on the same line.
One way in: the Middle Fork Snoqualmie road and trail from the Dingford Creek gate, leaving it at the steel bridge for Summit Chief Valley; the Northeast Face sibling uses the same trailhead.
The south-face line is reached only from Paradise via the Muir snowfield and the Cathedral Rocks notch; the Fryingpan Creek approach serves the east-side routes, not this face.

The Fryingpan Creek (Summerland) trailhead closed on 27 Sept 2026 for the bridge replacement, planned to last into 2029, so parties now walk the Wonderland Trail to Summerland from White River Campground; in winter and early season the climb is also approached from Paradise across the Cowlitz and Ingraham glaciers to the upper Whitman. White River Campground pin copied from sibling wa_mount_rainier_willis_wall; Paradise pin from sibling wa_little_tahoma_cowlitz_ingraham_glaciers.
Both Luahna rows start at the White River trailhead; this one goes via Boulder Basin and no second trailhead is used for this line.

Reached only by the PCT from the Snoqualmie Pass PCT North trailhead to Red Pass; no other trailhead serves the east ridge. Stored trailhead pin copied from the same-named trailhead on sibling wa_lundin_peak_south_face_left.
Royal Basin and the Home Lake / Royal Pass loop both start at the Upper Dungeness trailhead, so the alternative is a variation from the same start, not a second approach.
Both existing cards leave the same Dosewallips washout parking; the Constance Pass card simply continues farther up the closed road. One trailhead.
Same Dosewallips washout parking for the Lake Constance trail and the Constance Pass line; the cards already model the choice.
Lake Constance trail or Constance Pass, both from the same Dosewallips washout parking; no separate trailhead.
Both the Big Beaver/Access Creek line and the longer Little Beaver/Whatcom Pass line start from Ross Lake; the latter is a full-traverse option rather than a choice for a dedicated Fury trip.
Only the North Fork Quinault trail to the Sixteen Mile ford is described or used; no second trailhead for this scramble.
Both cards start at the Upper Dungeness trailhead; reaching Home Lake from the Dosewallips side is a much longer, rarely used option.

The stored Mowich Lake start has had no public road since the April 2025 Fairfax Bridge closure, and no established replacement approach (Carbon River railbed walk, a Westside Road traverse, or a carryover) is documented as what parties now use.
Westside Road walk to St Andrews Park and the Puyallup Cleaver is the only approach described or used.
The traditional Carbon River start is cut off by the permanent SR-165 Fairfax Bridge closure, leaving White River and the traverse under Curtis Ridge as the only practical approach.

The Chair 8 start is a seasonal ski variation from the ski area a short distance from the White Salmon lodge road start, not a separate approach. Stored pin taken from the row's own White Salmon Road (hairpin) trailhead waypoint.
One way in from the White Salmon lodge road; the Chair 8 traverse is a ski-season variant from essentially the same place.
The Putvin trail to Lake of the Angels is the standard approach; the Mildred Lakes card is a rarely used west-side option. Stored pin taken from the row's own Putvin trailhead waypoint.
Hoh River to Glacier Meadows and the Blue Glacier is the practical approach; the Bailey Range alternative is a multi-day off-trail traverse, not a real choice for a Mount Tom trip.
Traverse parties start through Boston Basin and the Taboo Glacier; no other trailhead.

The FR-2419 road-end start is the approach; reaching the summit from Ellinor is the separate ridge-traverse route, not another way onto this line. Stored pin taken from the row's own FR-2419 trailhead waypoint.
Single approach from the FR-38 gate at the Middle Fork Nooksack bridge up the logging roads; the Olivine scramble sibling shares the same gate. Stored pin from the row's own gate waypoint.
Climbed as a side trip off the Ptarmigan Traverse from Cascade Pass; no separate trailhead serves it.
Slate Pass is the only trailhead used; Monument Creek appears only in road notes. Stored pin taken from the row's own Slate Pass waypoint.
Dingford Creek, the closed road and a ford of the Middle Fork; Dutch Miller Gap is a landmark on that same approach.
Approached from Hannegan Pass over Easy Ridge, Perfect Pass and the Challenger Glacier; the Luna Cirque approaches from Big Beaver serve the cirque floor and Fury, not this line.
The East Slope is reached from Thunder Creek and Lucky Pass; the Eldorado Creek start serves the south ridge sibling, not this slope.
This line is the Crater Creek side; the Libby Creek approach belongs to the separate gully-ridge row, so the alternative card leads to the other route rather than onto this one.
The Libby Lake gully route is reached from the Libby Creek trailhead; the Crater Creek side is the separate southeast-ridge row. Stored pin taken from the row's own Libby Lake trailhead waypoint.
Esmeralda trailhead over Longs Pass to Ingalls Creek; Longs Pass is on the route, not a second trailhead.
Esmeralda trailhead over Longs Pass, shared with the East Ridge; no second trailhead.
Both cards use the Downey and Bachelor Creek approach; the second only differs in how the icefield is entered high on the mountain.
Downey and Bachelor Creek is the one practical approach; the two cards differ only in camp choice.
West-side routes are approached from Bedal Creek; the North Fork Sauk start, with its ford, serves the Corkscrew side.
Approached from Bedal Creek to the west-face meadows like the other west-face routes; no genuine second approach.
Off-trail from FR-63 by the North Fork Skykomish; the historic start from the North Fork road beyond Index is a dead-end, unused line. No coordinate is available for the stored pullout.

West Fork Buttermilk to Star Lake is the standard approach; the Lake Chelan boat to Prince Creek is a rarely used option mostly for multi-peak Sawtooth trips. Stored pin taken from the row's own trailhead waypoint.

All Chopping Block routes use the Goodell Creek and Terror Creek approach to the ridge camps. Stored pin copied from the same-named Goodell Creek Trailhead waypoint on sibling wa_the_chopping_block_south_route.

Same Goodell Creek approach as every Chopping Block route; the route starts up the lower Northeast Ridge but is not a finish of a separately approached line. Stored pin copied from the same-named Goodell Creek Trailhead waypoint on sibling wa_the_chopping_block_south_route.
Goodell Creek and Terror Creek is the only approach; the flagged prose compares routes, not approaches.
Over Cascade Pass to Trapper Lake is the practical approach; the Stehekin-valley card needs a boat or floatplane and is not a real choice for most parties.

The row's trailhead and prose describe Cascade Pass via Pelton Basin (card e1); the Stehekin-valley card needs a boat or floatplane and an obscure off-trail climb, so it is not a practical alternative.
The Upper Dungeness trail via Camp Handy and Boulder Shelter is the standard; reaching Home Lake from the Dosewallips washout is a much longer, rarely used alternative.
Both cards start at the same NF-77 pullout below the formation; one way in. No coordinate is available for the pullout on this row or its siblings.
Hannegan Pass and Easy Ridge to Perfect Pass is the standard; the Whatcom Pass low-orbit card also starts at Hannegan for nearly everyone, the Little Beaver start being a rare long option.
This row is itself one trailhead approach to Windy Peak (Iron Gate via the Boundary Trail); the other trailheads are separate sibling rows rather than ways onto this one.

Thirtymile up the Chewuch and Tungsten Creek trails to Tungsten Mine Camp is the documented approach; no second trailhead is described for this peak. Stored pin taken from the row's own Thirtymile waypoint.

The line starts at the toe of Dragontail's north buttress above Colchuck Lake, an alternate start to Triple Couloirs; it is reached only from the Stuart Lake trailhead via the Colchuck Lake trail, the same way in as every sibling route on the peak.

The usual and only described approach is from Paradise: Skyline Trail to Glacier Vista, across the Nisqually Glacier and up a snow chute onto the west side of the Wilson Glacier below the Wapowety Cleaver.
